LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: NOUNS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to identify items by name?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text
2. use different types of nouns in sentences
3. appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: NOUNS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: NOUNS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use different types of nouns in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use different types of nouns in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use different types of nouns in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use different types of nouns in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns to a partner. (skill: use different types of nouns in sentences)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text.
3. Practise this skill: use different types of nouns in sentences.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of correct grammar in written and spoken communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to identify items by name?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the different types of nouns from a print or digital text.
5. Be able to: use different types of nouns in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
